_about: Chapter C (Capabilities and protocol) of the suite results document: the prose data of DESIGN-DOC.md section 5 in R.json's format, written for the union of manifest v4 and v5 (the chapter's 12 scenarios, 2 families and 2 units are the same in both; v5 marks C-caps-0001 not implemented via MCP and C-caps-0003 as exposing its status only). `summary` and `coverage_gap` lead the chapter page, `intro` follows the computed lines; `families` keys on the family id, `units` on the unit id, `mcp_notes.units` holds the line under a unit whose MCP column is wholly not exercised. Every figure of the run is a placeholder (doc/facts.py) and every run-dependent sentence a conditional. The literal numbers are constants of the SPEC and of the manifest, listed under `_assumes`. Every claim follows SPEC-pattern-search.md sections 3 (transport), 6 (refusals), 10 and 23 (the capabilities documents), SPEC-labeled-traversal-core.md section 10.3, areas.py gen_C, checks.py and service_by_design.json. The catalogue entries this chapter needs beyond checks.json's: capabilities_doc, content_encoding, contains_source_context (checks-QCND.json); its by-design cases: cases.json (capabilities.not_expressible.protocol) and cases-QCND.json (the three capabilities document cases).

coverage_gap: *What remains unsupported.* Through the tools, nothing: the MCP tools call the service, which calls the host with its own client, so the content negotiation, the body's JSON form, the content type and the method cannot be chosen (`capabilities.not_expressible.protocol`), and no tool returns a host document as the host writes it: `traverse_capabilities` answers the service's view (`capabilities.traverse_capabilities_document`), `catalog` reshapes `GET /capabilities` into its backend entry (`capabilities.server_capabilities_document`) and nothing returns the pattern block (`capabilities.pattern_capabilities_document`); the fields `capabilities_doc` reads are not exposed there, so the MCP cells of C-caps read not exercised or inconclusive, and the document relations are not evaluated on that arm (a raw answer is missing). Every claim of this chapter therefore rests on the direct arms. [[n_footnoted ? intro: Three GET routes describe the host (SPEC-pattern-search section 23.1, SPEC-labeled-traversal-core section 10.3): `GET /capabilities`, the server document with its features, routes, identity (`release`, `server_instance`), the resolve bounds and the full pattern block as its `pattern` member; `GET /pattern/capabilities`, the full pattern block on its own (the contract version, availability, the graph's mode, mask and counting, the caps, the mismatch, predicate and genetic-code blocks); and `GET /traverse/capabilities`, the traversal probe document (identity, `k`, the limits, the attempts' server instance) whose `pattern` member is the gate block, the fields a client gates on with `details` naming the full block's route, and nothing else (section 23.2). A client gates by presence and value, never by a null read as false. The transport of `POST /pattern` (section 3): one RFC 8259 JSON text with unique member names and nothing after it, else 400 `invalid_request`; the answer compact JSON, gzip or deflate when `Accept-Encoding` asks; error bodies never compressed; a single-graph server answers on its graph. `/resolve` and `/traverse` share the request pool and the JSON rules.

Ground truth. The expectations of C-caps are the manifest's pinned facts of this index (`index_fp` as the pinned capabilities snapshot states it, `k` 31, regime and graph mode basic, mask file, counting exact, placement record, support `record_verified`, `pattern_contract_version` 1) and the SPEC's fixed values (`routes.pattern`, `details`); the three `same_answer` relations compare the documents with one another on the paths that must agree: `/capabilities` and `/traverse/capabilities` name the same server, `/capabilities`' pattern block is the `/pattern/capabilities` document, and the gate block projects it. C-protocol searches one 25 bp window of eco under each transport variant; the refusals carry the host's code, and the two GET-on-POST tests accept 400, 404 or 405.

Via MCP the chapter is out of reach by construction: the tools build the HTTP request themselves (headers, body, method), so no protocol scenario can be expressed, and the capabilities tools answer the service's own documents, which carry the service's gate, backends and presets, not the host's fields. Appendix B names the four cases.

C-caps.title: capabilities
C-caps.prose: The three documents, one test each (`capabilities_doc`): `/traverse/capabilities` states its identity and limits (`release`, `index_fp`, `k`, `max_query_bp`, `max_seeds`, the attempts' `server_instance`), the gate block with `pattern_contract_version` 1, `available` true and `details` naming `GET /pattern/capabilities`, `index_fp` equal to the pinned one, `k` 31 and `regime` basic, the whole within 32 KiB; `/pattern/capabilities` carries the full block (`caps`, `mismatches`, `predicate`, `genetic_codes`, `default_max_anchors`) with the index's graph mode, mask, counting, placement, support and the default projection; `/capabilities` is ready, in single mode, with its features, routes (the pattern routes named as section 23.1 says), the pattern block, the resolve bounds, `release` and `server_instance`. The relations (`same_answer` on named paths, printed under the table) tie the three together. [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} tests did not pass on every arm: {footnoted_text}. | In this run every test passed on every arm it was exercised on.]] [[n_relations ? Of the {n_relations:word} relations, {relations_text}.]] Via MCP the tools answer the service's own documents or nothing (see B); the host's fields the check reads are not in their answers, so no document claim is tested there[[n_mcp_not_exercised ?, and {n_mcp_not_exercised:word} test{n_mcp_not_exercised:s} [[n_mcp_not_exercised = 1 ? is | are]] not exercised at all]].
C-caps.claim: the three capabilities documents state the pinned identity, limits and gate block, agree with one another on their shared fields, and the probe document stays within 32 KiB

C-protocol.title: protocol
C-protocol.prose: The transport rules of section 3 and the refusals of section 6, one request each: `Accept-Encoding` gzip answers a gzip body (`content_encoding`) that still holds the window's contexts (`contains_source_context`), deflate a deflate body; an error body is never compressed (an unknown field under `Accept-Encoding` gzip: 400 `invalid_request` with no `Content-Encoding`); a JSON text with a comment, a duplicated member name and a body that is not an object are 400 `invalid_request`; a wrong `Content-Type` (text/plain) is still read as JSON (code-derived: the route parses the body whatever the header says); and GET on `POST /pattern` and on `POST /resolve` is not served (400, 404 or 405). The headers are read on the direct arms only. [[n_footnoted ? In this run {n_footnoted:word} of the {n_tests:word} tests did not pass on every arm: {footnoted_text}. | In this run every test passed on every arm it was exercised on.]] [[mcp_all_not_exercised ? Not exercised via MCP: the tools build the HTTP request themselves (see B). | Via MCP: {mcp_classes_text} (see B).]]
C-protocol.claim: the host negotiates gzip and deflate, never compresses an error body, refuses non-RFC 8259 JSON and non-object bodies, reads JSON under a wrong content type and does not serve GET on a POST route
